title: Pay-television uplink override
summary: A teleport engineer overpowered a pay-television channel's uplink for several minutes to display a protest message. He was identified and prosecuted.

sources.title: US court records, United States v. MacDougall

title: Interference with two US Earth-observation satellites
summary: A US congressional commission reported that two civil Earth-observation satellites experienced interference through a commercial ground station; for one, the responsible party completed every step needed to command it but issued no commands.

sources.title: US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, 2011 Annual Report to Congress

title: Crackdown on misuse of military UHF transponders
summary: Brazilian police acted against dozens of people using modified radios to talk through ageing military communications satellites that relayed any signal in band.

sources.title: Wired, The Great Brazilian Sat-Hack Crackdown

title: Research into satellite terminal firmware
summary: A researcher reported hard-coded credentials, undocumented protocols and other flaws across widely used maritime, aviation and military terminals, and later showed some could be reached from the internet.

sources.title: IOActive, A Wake-up Call for SATCOM Security (2014) and Last Call for SATCOM Security (2018)

title: Breach of a weather agency's satellite data network
summary: A US weather agency took satellite data feeds offline for unscheduled maintenance after an intrusion. Officials told the press the attack came from China; no formal attribution followed.

sources.title: Washington Post reporting, November 2014

title: Satellite links used to hide espionage infrastructure
summary: Researchers described an espionage group receiving stolen data by listening to other customers' unencrypted satellite internet downlinks across a wide beam.

sources.title: Kaspersky GReAT, Satellite Turla: APT Command and Control in the Sky

title: Espionage campaign reaches a satellite operator
summary: A security vendor reported a group inside a satellite communications operator that appeared most interested in the systems that monitor and control satellites.

sources.title: Symantec, Thrip: Espionage Group Hits Satellite, Telecoms, and Defense Companies

title: Research: reading geostationary broadband traffic
summary: A researcher showed that inexpensive home television equipment could capture unencrypted maritime, aviation and enterprise traffic from eighteen geostationary satellites.

sources.title: J. Pavur, Whispers Among the Stars, Black Hat USA 2020

title: Ransomware at a space-agency IT contractor
summary: A ransomware crew published files it said came from a contractor providing IT services to a space agency.

sources.title: ZDNet reporting on DoppelPaymer claims, June 2020

title: KA-SAT terminal wipe
summary: Intruders used a misconfigured remote-access appliance to reach the management segment of a broadband satellite network and issued destructive commands that overwrote flash memory in tens of thousands of modems across Europe, also cutting remote monitoring of thousands of wind turbines.

sources.title: Viasat, KA-SAT Network cyber attack overview (30 March 2022)
SentinelLabs, AcidRain: A Modem Wiper Rains Down on Europe

title: Claimed intrusion at a national space agency
summary: A hacktivist group published files and claimed to have disrupted a vehicle-monitoring system at Russia's space agency; the agency denied that control systems were affected.

sources.title: Media reporting of NB65 claims, March 2022

title: Jamming of commercial satellite broadband in Ukraine
summary: Terminals supplied to Ukraine were jammed near the front line. The operator changed software within days, and US defence officials later cited the speed of that response.

sources.title: US Department of Defense remarks reported by Breaking Defense, April 2022

title: Research: fault injection on a broadband user terminal
summary: A researcher bypassed secure boot on a consumer satellite terminal with a custom board that glitches the power supply, gaining code execution on the device.

sources.title: L. Wouters, Glitched on Earth by Humans, Black Hat USA 2022

title: Claimed denial of service against a broadband constellation's sign-in
summary: A pro-Russian collective claimed to have made a satellite broadband provider's customer sign-in unreachable for several hours.

sources.title: Trustwave SpiderLabs reporting, November 2022

title: Intrusion at a US satellite communications provider
summary: Government incident responders said they found a Russian military intelligence group in the network of a satellite communications provider serving critical-infrastructure customers; it had been present for months.

sources.title: CyberScoop, CISA researchers: Russia's Fancy Bear infiltrated US satellite network

title: Espionage campaign against Russian aerospace
summary: A vendor described a group using phishing and custom backdoors against aerospace organisations over several years.

sources.title: Positive Technologies, Space Pirates

title: Claimed tampering with exposed navigation receivers
summary: A hacktivist group posted screenshots it said showed access to internet-exposed satellite navigation receivers and deletion of their data.

sources.title: Cyble research blog, March 2023

title: Research: on-orbit takeover demonstration
summary: At a security conference, a company team showed it could take control of functions on an experimental agency nanosatellite, alter imagery and hide the changes, working with the agency throughout.

sources.title: Thales, CYSAT 2023 demonstration on ESA OPS-SAT

title: Research: security analysis of satellite firmware
summary: Academics analysed three real satellite firmware images and found missing command protection and exploitable flaws, alongside a survey showing how often designers rely on obscurity.

sources.title: J. Willbold et al., Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites, IEEE S&P 2023

title: Outage at a Russian satellite communications provider
summary: A provider serving government and energy customers went offline. Unidentified actors claimed to have damaged terminals and leaked files; measurements confirmed the outage.

sources.title: The Record, Hackers claim to take down Russian satellite communications provider

title: Exercise: first capture-the-flag on a satellite in orbit
summary: Finalist teams in a government-sponsored contest attacked and defended a purpose-built cubesat in orbit, the first such event on a live spacecraft.

sources.title: Hack-A-Sat 4 final event on Moonlighter, DEF CON 31

title: Password-spray campaign including the satellite sector
summary: A vendor observed thousands of organisations targeted with password spraying, with follow-on intrusion at a small number in the satellite, defence and pharmaceutical sectors.

sources.title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence, Peach Sandstorm password spray campaigns

title: Breach at Japan's space agency
summary: The agency disclosed unauthorised access to its central directory server, reportedly through a network-device flaw, and later reported further attacks in 2024. It said launch and satellite operations data were not affected.

sources.title: JAXA statements and Japanese government briefings, 2023 to 2024

title: Persistent navigation interference affecting aviation and shipping
summary: Aircraft and ships around the Baltic, Black Sea and Middle East reported daily jamming and spoofing of satellite navigation. Several European governments raised the matter with international bodies.

sources.title: EASA and IATA statements on GNSS interference, 2024

title: New variant of the modem wiper appears
summary: Researchers found a broader successor to the 2022 modem wiper, able to target more embedded device types, around the time of outages at Ukrainian providers.

sources.title: SentinelLabs, AcidPour: New Embedded Wiper Variant of AcidRain

title: Interference with European broadcast satellites
summary: Operators and several European states reported uplink interference that disrupted or replaced television programming; the ITU's Radio Regulations Board called for it to stop.

sources.title: ITU Radio Regulations Board decisions, 2024

title: Custom backdoor used against satellite and communications-equipment firms
summary: A vendor reported a new multi-stage backdoor deployed against satellite, communications-equipment, energy and government targets, with attacker infrastructure hosted in fraudulently obtained cloud subscriptions.

sources.title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence, Peach Sandstorm deploys new custom Tickler malware

title: Claimed cut of satellite communications on Iranian ships
summary: A group claimed to have disabled satellite terminals on 116 tankers and cargo ships by attacking the systems of their communications provider, and claimed a repeat later in the year.

sources.title: The Maritime Executive, Cyber Hackers Claim to Have Disabled Iranian Ship Communications

title: Intrusion at Poland's space agency
summary: The agency disconnected its network from the internet after detecting unauthorised access to its IT systems, and national cyber services were brought in.

sources.title: Statements by the Polish Space Agency and the Minister for Digital Affairs, March 2025

title: Telecom espionage campaign reaches a satellite operator
summary: Press reports named a satellite operator among the victims of a state espionage campaign against communications carriers. The company confirmed unauthorised access through a compromised device and reported no customer impact.

sources.title: Via Satellite, Viasat confirms unauthorized access after Bloomberg report of Salt Typhoon impact

title: Surge of operations against the space sector during the Israel-Iran war
summary: A researcher counted more than 67 claimed operations by 25 actors against space organisations during the twelve-day conflict, mostly denial of service and data-leak claims.

sources.title: Via Satellite, The Space Sector Under Cyber Fire in the US-Israel-Iran War

title: Research: sensitive links found unencrypted on geostationary satellites
summary: University researchers scanning geostationary satellites with consumer equipment found a large share of links unencrypted, including mobile-network backhaul, corporate and government traffic.

sources.title: UC San Diego and University of Maryland, Don't Look Up, ACM CCS 2025

title: Data theft from a space agency's external servers
summary: A seller claimed roughly 200 GB including source code and access tokens taken from collaboration servers. The agency said the affected servers were outside its corporate network and held unclassified material; a further, larger theft was claimed afterwards.

sources.title: Space.com, Cyberthieves hit European Space Agency, stealing hundreds of gigabytes of data

title: Claimed intrusions at Gulf satellite operators
summary: During the 2026 conflict a persona claimed to have disrupted infrastructure, intercepted communications and deleted data at several Gulf satellite companies and a space agency. One screen recording lent partial support; other claims are unverified. No spacecraft were reported affected.

sources.title: Via Satellite, The Space Sector Under Cyber Fire in the US-Israel-Iran War

title: Intimidation messages to aerospace employees
summary: Employees of an aerospace prime based in Israel received text messages claiming their personal data had been breached and urging them to leave.

sources.title: Via Satellite, The Space Sector Under Cyber Fire in the US-Israel-Iran War

title: Extortion crews and access brokers concentrate on suppliers
summary: The sector's sharing centre tracked close to seventy claimed attacks, over half on manufacturers, contractors and integrators, with identity theft, session hijacking and help-desk deception as common ways in. Operators separately reported activity at four times its pre-war level.

sources.title: Space ISAC, Threat Briefing 46
Via Satellite, Space Sector Faces 400% Surge in Cyberattacks Amid Iran War
